chunks: Hariz narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that he said:

There is no owner of wealth, of gold or silver, who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will confine him on the Day of Resurrection in a flat open plain and set over him a bald serpent pursuing him while he shrinks away from it. Then when he sees that he cannot escape from it, he will let it seize his hand, and it will gnaw it as a radish is gnawed; then it will become a collar around his neck. And that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
"They shall be encircled by what they were stingy with on the Day of Resurrection."

And there is no owner of wealth consisting of camels, cattle, or sheep who withholds the zakat of his wealth, except that Allah will confine him on the Day of Resurrection in a flat open plain; every hoofed creature will tread upon him with its hoof, and every fanged creature will bite him with its fang.

And there is no owner of wealth consisting of date-palms, grapevines, or crops who withholds its zakat, except that Allah, Exalted is He, will collar him with the produce of his land down to seven earths until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection when people are judged
key_terms.بَخِلُوا: they acted stingily and withheld what was due
key_terms.رَيْعَةَ أَرْضِهِ: the yield or produce of his land
key_terms.زَكَاةَ: the obligatory alms due upon wealth
key_terms.شُجَاعًا أَقْرَعَ: a bald serpent used here as a form of punishment
key_terms.طَوْقًا: a collar fastened around the neck
key_terms.يَحِيدُ: he recoils or turns away in fear

ai.seo_question: What happens to a person who refuses to pay zakat according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith warns of severe punishment in the afterlife for those who withhold zakat from monetary wealth, livestock, and agricultural produce. It links the punishment directly to Qur'anic imagery, showing that miserliness in obligatory charity becomes a cause of humiliation and torment on the Day of Resurrection. The narration underscores the grave religious and moral seriousness of fulfilling zakat obligations.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1583 Hariz reported from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he said:

"Anyone who possesses wealth in gold or silver and withholds the Zakat of his wealth will be confined by Allah (swt), the Almighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection in a flat, open plain. A bald snake will be unleashed upon him, chasing him as he attempts to flee. When he realizes he cannot escape, the snake will seize his hand and bite it like a radish is bitten, and then it will coil around his neck. This is the meaning of Allah’s (swt) statement:
'They will be encircled by what they withheld on the Day of Resurrection' (Surah Ali ‘Imran 3:180).

And anyone who possesses wealth in the form of camels, cows, or sheep and withholds the Zakat of his wealth will be confined by Allah (swt), the Almighty, on the Day of Resurrection in a flat, open plain. Every animal with a hoof will trample upon him with its hooves, and every animal with fangs will bite him with its fangs.

And anyone who possesses wealth in the form of palm trees, grapevines, or crops and withholds its Zakat, Allah (swt), the Exalted, will place upon him the burden of the yield of his land, extending to the depth of seven earths, until the Day of Resurrection."
